design_summary.purpose: A small SRAM scratchpad controller that demonstrates integration of a prebuilt Sky130 SRAM macro and MBIST collateral while remaining simple for fast RTL, synthesis, and DFT validation runs.
design_summary.operating_model: The controller exposes a register-style local management interface for firmware to read/write controller state and access a 256x32 scratchpad memory through a single functional access path. It also provides explicit BIST request, status, and interrupt signaling so downstream MBIST agents can detect SRAM macro intent and attach collateral without changing the top-level controller contract.

external_interfaces.name: clk
external_interfaces.purpose: Primary clock for controller and memory wrapper/model operation.

external_interfaces.name: reset_n
external_interfaces.purpose: Active-low reset that clears controller state and places the memory path in a safe deselected state.

external_interfaces.name: wr_en
external_interfaces.purpose: Write strobe for register programming and control updates.

external_interfaces.name: rd_en
external_interfaces.purpose: Read strobe for register and memory-visible readback paths.

external_interfaces.name: bist_start
external_interfaces.purpose: Top-level BIST request input for explicit memory test integration.

external_interfaces.name: rd_data
external_interfaces.purpose: Software-visible read data from register and memory readback paths.

external_interfaces.name: irq
external_interfaces.purpose: Interrupt output asserted when enabled and BIST status is latched.

module_architecture.name: sram_mbist_demo_controller
module_architecture.role: Top-level SRAM scratchpad controller with internal register map, software-accessible memory operations, BIST request/status handling, and a child SRAM wrapper instance named u_sram.
responsibilities: Decode the external write/read strobes and local register addresses.
Maintain control, status, memory address, memory write-data, memory read-data, BIST control, BIST status, and IRQ status state.
Drive the SRAM wrapper interface through one functional access path.
Expose software-visible read data from register and memory readback paths.
Provide explicit BIST request and status signaling for downstream MBIST collateral generation.
Assert irq only when IRQ_ENABLE is set and a BIST completion or failure status is latched.
interface_notes: Must receive clk, reset_n, wr_en, wr_addr, wr_data, rd_en, rd_addr, and bist_start.
Must drive rd_data, ready, bist_done, bist_fail, and irq.
Instantiates demo_sram_32x256_wrapper as child memory wrapper instance u_sram.
Uses inter-module signals sram_csb, sram_web, sram_addr, sram_din, and sram_dout as the explicit memory contract.
Reset clears CONTROL, STATUS, MEM_ADDR, MEM_WDATA, MEM_RDATA, MEM_CONTROL, BIST_CONTROL, BIST_STATUS, IRQ_STATUS, ready, bist_done, bist_fail, irq, and internal busy or pending state.
ownership_notes: sram_csb, sram_web, sram_addr, and sram_din are owned by the controller and sourced from its register and access sequencing logic.
rd_data, ready, bist_done, bist_fail, and irq are controller-owned outputs.
sram_dout is owned by the wrapper side and observed by the controller for readback and software-visible MEM_RDATA capture.

module_architecture.name: demo_sram_32x256_wrapper
module_architecture.role: Functional scratchpad wrapper that exposes the canonical SRAM access interface and binds to the qualified Sky130 SRAM macro when available or to the synthesizable fallback model when collateral is unavailable.
responsibilities: Allow safe binding to the prebuilt Sky130 SRAM macro when available.
Allow fallback to the synthesizable memory model when macro collateral is unavailable.
Preserve functional read/write behavior for integration and simulation.
interface_notes: Ports are clk, csb, web, addr[7:0], din[31:0], and dout[31:0].
The controller instantiates this wrapper as u_sram to preserve memory macro detectability.
The wrapper may bind to the prebuilt Sky130 macro or to demo_sram_32x256_model without changing the interface.
If the underlying macro has a second read port, it is to be tied off safely or left reserved for MBIST wrapper integration; the controller uses one functional access path.
ownership_notes: clk, csb, web, addr, and din are wrapper inputs derived from controller-owned signals or the macro binding path.

module_architecture.name: demo_sram_32x256_model
module_architecture.role: Synthesizable fallback memory model with the same interface as the wrapper, intended for simulation and synthesis when prebuilt macro collateral is unavailable.
responsibilities: Match the wrapper port list exactly.
Remain compatible with synthesis and simulation flows without vendor-specific primitives.
interface_notes: Ports are clk, csb, web, addr[7:0], din[31:0], and dout[31:0].
This model is fallback only and keeps the same functional wrapper interface so AutoMBIST can replace or wrap the path.
No vendor-only primitives are used in the fallback path.
ownership_notes: clk, csb, web, addr, and din are model inputs.

interface_summary.intent: Controller drives a single functional access path into the SRAM wrapper for scratchpad reads and writes, keeping macro intent explicit for downstream synthesis and MBIST collateral generation.
Wrapper returns read data to the controller so MEM_RDATA and software-visible readback can be updated.
Fallback model uses the same interface and signal semantics as the wrapper, enabling simulation and synthesis when the prebuilt macro collateral is unavailable.
Global clock fanout for controller sequencing and memory access timing.
Clock is shared with the memory wrapper binding for synchronous access behavior.
Clock is shared with the synthesizable fallback model for synchronous access behavior.
Active-low reset clears controller registers, status, and interrupt state.
External BIST request input is consumed by the controller BIST request path.

data_flow_summary: Firmware programs MEM_ADDR and MEM_WDATA, then uses MEM_CONTROL to request SRAM writes through the wrapper-controlled functional path.
Firmware programs MEM_ADDR and uses MEM_CONTROL to request SRAM reads; the controller captures the wrapper read data into MEM_RDATA and exposes it through rd_data.
CONTROL.ENABLE gates normal controller operation, CONTROL.SOFT_RESET requests a software-visible reset action, and CONTROL.IRQ_ENABLE arms interrupt generation.
BIST_CONTROL.START or the external bist_start input initiates a BIST request path; BIST_CONTROL.CLEAR_RESULT clears latched BIST state.
BIST_STATUS reports done, fail, running, and last_fail_addr[7:0] so MBIST agents can observe or replace the memory path without changing the controller contract.
IRQ_STATUS latches bist_done and bist_fail events until cleared by IRQ_CLEAR, and irq asserts only when IRQ_ENABLE is set and a latched BIST event is present.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single-clock design using clk for the controller and the memory wrapper/model interface. The top-level memory access path is synchronous and intentionally simple for fast integration and DFT detection.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: On reset, the controller clears CONTROL, STATUS, MEM_ADDR, MEM_WDATA, MEM_RDATA, MEM_CONTROL, BIST_CONTROL, BIST_STATUS, IRQ_STATUS, ready, bist_done, bist_fail, irq, and any internal busy or pending state. The memory wrapper is held in a safe deselected state during reset.

integration_notes: The structured memory macro contract identifies sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 as a prebuilt Sky130 SRAM with depth 256, data width 32, address width 8, instance name u_sram, and requires_mbist=true.
The controller RTL must instantiate demo_sram_32x256_wrapper as child memory wrapper instance u_sram to preserve memory macro detectability.
The wrapper may bind to the qualified Sky130 SRAM macro or to demo_sram_32x256_model depending on available collateral; the top-level controller interface must not change.
The functional wrapper interface is clk, csb, web, addr[7:0], din[31:0], and dout[31:0].
The fallback demo_sram_32x256_model is simulation/synthesis fallback only and must keep the same interface so AutoMBIST can replace or wrap the path.
The design remains descriptive of a single functional access path, while leaving room for a second read port on the underlying macro to be safely tied off or reserved for MBIST wrapper integration.
Register map coverage includes CONTROL, STATUS, MEM_ADDR, MEM_WDATA, MEM_RDATA, MEM_CONTROL, BIST_CONTROL, BIST_STATUS, IRQ_STATUS, and IRQ_CLEAR exactly as specified.

The requested deliverables include synthesizable SystemVerilog, register map, assertions, simulation testbench, UPF-lite collateral, timing constraints, and packaging manifest; this document preserves the architecture intent without redefining hierarchy or interfaces.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
